analysis:
ModelLoadAdmission.swift changes are comment-only. SystemMemory.swift changes the default reclaimable availability math to max(free+inactive, free−speculative+external+purgeable). Sampling failure behavior (nil, or 0 for free-only) and the invalid-env-value-falls-to-free-only rule are preserved. The finding is that the larger default credit can over-admit loads on shared hosts.

GLM5NextManagedLoad.swift adds phase timing and logging, which expose only the model id and counts. It also drops the page cache for the .safetensors files after a successful load. It publishes `verifiedArtifactSHA256` as `plan.weights.manifest.aggregateSHA256`, the catalog-pinned value, rather than a recomputed hash. This is only valid if the native `GLM5NextArtifactLoader` really SHA-256-verifies every core file, as the comment at line 284 says. That reader is not in the supplied evidence, so I could not verify the claim. Integration should confirm that the consumer of `verifiedArtifactSHA256` (weight-hash attestation to the coordinator, T-012/T-027) cannot report the pinned hash after a partial or failed verification. It should also confirm the recheck covers file identity between hashing and payload read.

DeadlineRuntimeEnvironment.swift adds `DARKBLOOM_VERIFIED_WEIGHTS_FILE` to the operational keys, which exempts it from the qualification scrub. Whatever reads that file is not visible here. If the file lets the provider skip re-hashing or influences the reported weight hash, an operator-controlled path would be a T-012 forgery vector, and treating it as non-performance-affecting would be wrong. Needs a check of the reader and writer for file ownership, permissions and binding to the file identities.

FlintResponseFormat.swift removes `requireExplicitTypes`, so untyped json_schema leaves are now inferred as string and silently narrow output constraints. I regard this as a correctness change, not a security regression. Only the file metadata unit was supplied, so I could not check it against the full source.

findings.detail: On the default `reclaimable` policy, `availableBytes` now returns max(free+inactive, free−speculative+external_page_count+purgeable_count) (SystemMemory.swift lines 60-62, 83-86). `external_page_count` covers every pageable file-backed page, including actively mapped pages that other processes or this process are still using, plus dirty pages that need writeback. The code comment claims reclaiming this memory never compresses or swaps process memory. That holds only for unmapped clean cache. Active mapped pages must be refaulted, and dirty pages need writeback first. The value feeds `ModelLoadAdmission.freeForLoadGb`/`maxLoadableWeightGb`, which clamp the load gate and the advertised loadable weight. Heavy file-cache or mapped-file use on a shared host can therefore inflate the headroom, so the provider admits a load or KV growth that pushes the machine into swap or OOM pressure and degrades availability. The cost is lost availability and over-advertised capacity. Mitigation: credit only a conservative fraction of `external_page_count`, or only inactive file pages, or keep the stricter policy on shared hosts. The existing `free-only` option remains available.
findings.title: Default reclaimable policy now credits all file-backed and purgeable pages as available memory, loosening the load/KV admission clamp
